arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Mr. Unikowsky argued the statute specifies a 30-day tolling period after dismissal.
Ms. Alikhan argued dismissed claims are treated as never filed without a mechanism.
Justice Alito questioned whether the statute includes stop-the-clock state statutes.
Justice Sotomayor noted Congress rejected the ALI report's grace period language.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: This case examines the scope of a federal statute governing supplemental jurisdiction. The core issue is the definition of tolling under Title 28 Section 1367(d). the side that brought the case argues the statute creates a mandatory 30-day grace period. the opposing side contends the statute only incorporates existing state tolling laws. The Court must interpret the statutory text and its legislative history.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: Litigants face uncertainty about deadlines to refile dismissed claims in state court. A uniform federal deadline provides consistent protection for federal litigants. State-specific rules create varying deadlines across jurisdictions. The interpretation determines the practical time available to pursue legal remedies. This affects access to state courts for dismissed federal claims.
